title: Pluripotent stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles for systemic immune modulation in diabetes therapy - Nature Nanotechnology
byline: Zarubova; Jana; Hasani-Sadrabadi; Mohammad Mahdi; Wu; Yutong; Diamante; Graciel; Cheng; Jenny; Park; Soomin; Han; Majedi; Fatemeh Sadat; Yang; Wang; Olivia; Ahn
html:
Abstract

Embryonic development is characterized by remarkable immune tolerance, yet whether this property extends to pluripotent stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) has remained unclear. Here we show that EVs from pluripotent stem cells (PSCs), including embryonic stem cells and induced pluripotent stem cells, outperform mesenchymal stem cell-derived EVs in suppressing proinflammatory cytokine secretion, reducing T cell activation and inducing regulatory T cells. PSC EVs display distinct molecular signatures, containing unique proteins and microRNAs absent from mesenchymal stem cell-derived EVs, including the pluripotency-associated proteins ROR1 and CD133 and members of the miR-302 family. Dynamic suspension culture of PSC aggregates enhances the EV yield, providing a scalable and reproducible source. Delivered via a biomaterial scaffold, two local injections of induced PSC EVs significantly improved diabetes-free survival in an antigen-specific type 1 diabetes model, increasing regulatory T cell populations in draining lymph nodes, as well as inducing systemic immune modulation and preserving β-cell mass. These findings establish PSC EVs as a scalable immunomodulatory platform for autoimmune disease and for immune tolerance in cell therapy.

Data availability

The main data supporting the results in this study are available within the Article and its Supplementary Information. The scRNA-seq data are available in the Gene Expression Omnibus under accession GSE291555. Mass spectrometry proteomics data have been deposited in the ProteomeXchange Consortium via the PRIDE partner repository under accession PXD082874. Source data are provided with this paper.
